## v1.2.13 (planned, 2026-10-11)

Contraction: fewer lines, no behaviour change, with v1.2.12's tests and checked models as the net under it. Passes in this order, one writer per package: remove dead and stale code; adopt the Go standard library or established packages where they replace hand-rolled code; run go fix (and gopls modernize) over all Go code; pull code the tools share into modules, then code the modules share into modules; make each test minimal, on test frameworks and shared helper modules. The module pass also covers the copies across the two repositories: 59 same-named packages exist as separate copies in nova-sprint and nova-tools (about 71,500 shared lines, measured 2026-10-11 at nova-sprint 15c779c and nova-tools 2a648d8). Each gets one owner, nova-sprint as with nova-roadmap, and the other repository imports it: the identical copies first, then the diverged ones (member, fleet, cardtree, tool, and parts of friend and swarm), reconciled under v1.2.12's tests. The first named entries are the nova-roadmap extraction and the brief boilerplate moving into the card contract. Measured as lines per repository and package, product against test, from a baseline taken before the first pass.

- **A worker's stop on needs that have not landed is a coordination failure, never the worker's; the needs withdrawal goes working -> waiting** (planned). Blocker. A worker that stops because its card's named needs have not landed was blamed: the finish read its HOLD ("the base lacks ...") as a brief defect, or as failed work. A failed finish whose primary has a named need (not waived) that has not landed at the finish (stoppedOnNeeds, needs_stop.go; the table's facts, never the report's words) is now a coordination failure, judged before the brief defect: the work card goes back to the pool at a new generation (no fail mark and no ok% hit on the worker's row, no redeal spent, counted neither ok nor failed in the route and model stats), the primary goes working -> waiting at once, and one happened note, "a card returned: dealt before its needs landed", names the needs and the report (needsStopReturned); no brief-defect, failed-work or invariant judgment is written. The next deal after the needs land cuts the next attempt: an attempt number is spent, never a redeal or a failure. A primary is returned this way at most MaxNeedsReturns (3) times (needs_returns); past that, and whenever every need has landed by the finish, the HOLD is judged as any other, so a stale base never loops unseen (the cold read's probe: twelve free rounds). No coordination-failure counter exists, so the stop is classed as not the worker's. The needs withdrawal of a dealt card (needsWithdrawals) moved its working primary working -> waiting with no lifecycle row, so the store refused it; the lifecycle now has that row (withdraw, its needs have not landed, carried by the move's needs field), and needsWaits moves a ready primary whose needs have not landed and whose work card is dealt nowhere ready -> waiting. tla/SprintTables.tla models both (NeedsWithdraw, NeedsWait; WorkingToWaitingOnlyOnNeeds, NeedsWithdrawalWaits, ReadyToWaitingOnlyByInsert widened to needs) with the reversed witness withdrawready (the withdrawal run working -> ready breaks NeedsWithdrawalWaits, rule 11). docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md (the lifecycle table; needs and the deal; a brief defect) states the rule. Tests: TestAStopOnUnlandedNeedsIsNotTheWorkers, TestACardWithdrawnForItsNeedsIsDealtWhenTheyLand, TestProbe96LandedNeedHoldLoopsUnbounded, TestProbe96UnrelatedNotLandedWordsSkipTheFailure, and the needs tests held to the lifecycle (lawfulDeal) and the end-of-tick check. From: hand/take-and-deal-honour-needs (PR 96), 2026-10-11, after two cold reads (HOLD); the owner: "Blocker bug to fix that please." (schema msg2/msg3 cards in every language dealt before their msg1 and t09/t10 needs landed; the worker stopped and the server blamed her); code read at nova-sprint main 93c84c63.
- **Extract the roadmap tool into nova-roadmap** (planned). The roadmap and fixes code exists twice: here as internal/roadmap, internal/roadmapdoc, tools/roadmap and the nova-work roadmap verbs (about 3,100 lines with their tests), and in nova-tools as internal/roadmap, internal/roadmap/sexp and tools/roadmap (about 1,300 lines with their tests, about 930 without), with two diverging copies of the generator. Unify the s-expression format first; then one module and one CLI, nova-roadmap, living in this repository (a module and cmd/nova-roadmap): it reads and writes the data, renders ROADMAP.md and FIXES.md, and runs the sync check. Both repositories use it and delete their own copies: this one its internal copies, nova-tools by importing nova-roadmap from this repository. Net fewer lines. Its s-expressions stay importable later as a node by nova-work; that import is a v1.3 item, not this one. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: v1.2.13 contraction, pass 4 (shared code into modules); nova-roadmap lives in nova-sprint.
- **Brief boilerplate moves into the card contract** (planned). A brief names the card contract instead of carrying its text, so briefs are shorter and the contract has one copy. The RULES, LEDGERS, WALL AND TOOLS and BUDGET blocks, about 6 KB of every 10 to 11 KB brief, are referenced once from the card contract instead of repeated in each brief, and a card lint refuses repeated instruction text in a brief. Agreed with the owner on 2026-10-11 as a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai). From: roadmap item briefs-by-reference.
- **The idle alarm is raised once an episode, with a test that drives the ticks** (planned). TestTheIdleAlarmNamesTheRootsOnceAnEpisode (internal/sprint/store/idle_test.go) was red on main and red in every PR's CI: it still expected the older rule, where every end of an idle episode pushed the working-again note. b34ff36f chose the end note by cause (idleEnd): only the fleet working at half its width again says working again, and an episode that ends because no card waits pushes the fleet's idle episode ended, naming that (docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 14). The test now pins that rule. A new test, TestTheIdleAlarmIsRaisedOnceAnEpisodeNeverOncePerTick (internal/sprint/idle_test.go), drives 15-second ticks over an idle fleet and checks the count after every tick: none under the window, exactly one at the window and for the rest of the episode (never zero, never two), one working-again note when the fleet works, and exactly one more alarm in the next episode. The reversed witness for one alarm a tick already exists and passes as a witness: tla/MCSprintRulesIdleBrokenEveryTick.cfg (AlarmOncePerEpisode). The seat's flood of the fleet works below its alarm judgment (alarms.go, the alarm_fleet threshold) is a different alarm from the idle note: it is keyed by type alone, one judgment while it stands, and TestBacklogAlarmsPushOncePerEpisodeFromConfigThresholds holds it to one an episode on the twin store. The flood was not reproduced from the code at main, so the live cause is still open (a judgment closed or answered between ticks, or a server build older than main, are the candidates); it needs a read of the live judgment log, which this change does not touch. From: the owner and the seat, 2026-10-11: the idle alarm flooded the seat and the idle test was red on main.
- **Done is every card a row completed, and the readers' verdict counts the reads the accept counts** (planned). Pull request 94. Friend stella's row read done 0 and ok% 0.0% while the log recorded her finishes ok and their reads ok: the readers' verdict (TickVerdicts) read the readers table alone, keyed an ok by the read's row and used the tier's read count, while the accept also counts the fleet table's read cards, retired off their rows with their verdicts, by the reader, at the sprint's count. The accept and the verdict now count from one function (standingReads). A row's done, a friend's or a member's, is every card it completed, of every kind registered in sprint.DoneKinds (a work card the readers' verdict moved to ok, a fix card likewise, a read card completed with a verdict, ok or broken; a returned read completes nothing; a merge card is one more entry once merges are dealt cards), counted from the log lines that complete them through the done record (store.keepDone, store.DoneSince), keyed by epoch and counted from a stats reset's mark. ok% stays the work's measure, the readers' verdicts on the row's work. tla/ReadVerdict.tla models the verdict against the accept. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: "The dashboard has to reflect the truth." and "Done is every card completed."; root cause found by Stella.
- **A landing the hook gate refuses does not roll a switch back** (planned). BLOCKER. server switch --rollback --window 30m restarts the server, the restart ends the seat's hook (the seat hook record says state=gone, why=the server restarted), and the new server's first landing pass, run as the coordinator before the seat hooks in again, is refused by the hook gate (nova-sprint land REFUSED: You must hook in first: run nova-sprint hook). landOnce counted any nonzero exit of the landing as a land failure and asked CheckRollbackOnLandFailure, and the store's open refuses through refuse, exit 2, the code of a pass fault, so the v1.2.12 switch rolled itself back to v1.2.11 1.5 seconds after it began; every switch with --rollback met the race. The hook gate's refusal is now the typed error hookGateError (coordinator.go coordinatorGate; storeCtx returns it), land reports it to landOnce through the app.land seam (cmdLand is unchanged for the command line, exit 2 and the same words), and landOnce, on it, does not ask the rollback check: the window, the binary and the switch state stay as they were, the pass prints one line, LAND WAITS for the seat's hook: <the gate's sentence>; nothing was landed, and the next pass tries again, and the loop's next pass is LandEvery as before, so it neither spins nor waits longer. The refusal is found by errors.As, never by its words. Only a landing that was let through and failed counts toward the rollback. Tests in cmd/nova-sprint/landloop_hookgate_test.go: TestAHookGateRefusalInTheWindowIsNotARollback (three passes in the window refused by the gate: no SERVER ROLLBACK, the switch stands, the state file is kept, one waits line each pass, the card is still queued; then, the seat hooked in, a failing landing rolls back), TestARealLandFailureInTheWindowStillRollsBack and, in hookgate_error_test.go, TestTheHookGateRefusalIsATypedError. tla/ServerSwitch.tla gains hooked, SwitchRestart, SeatHooksIn and LandHookRefused, every landing outcome now guarded by hooked, the invariant NoRollbackOnAHookRefusal and the reversed witness hookfault (MCServerSwitchBrokenHookfault, which counts the refusal as a land fault and rolls the switch back), run with TLC on hetzner2. docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 14 states the rule where the switch and its window are described. From: this card, a hand fix by the coordinator's child, 2026-10-11 ~21:00Z; the v1.2.12 switch (nova-sprint server switch --rollback --window 30m): SEAT HOOK state=gone why=the server restarted, then nova-sprint land REFUSED: You must hook in first, then SERVER ROLLBACK to v1.2.11 1.5 s later; code read at nova-sprint main f94ea09c (cmd/nova-sprint/landloop.go landOnce, internal/sprint/server_switch.go CheckRollbackOnLandFailure).
- **A landing whose every conflict is a shared ledger lands** (planned). Measured over 60 minutes of the live sprint on 2026-10-11: about 300 landing refusals against about 35 landings, most of them conflicts in the shared ledgers alone (docs/fixes.sexp, FIXES.md, tla/COVERAGE.tsv, tla/RUNS.tsv, tla/CASES.tsv, and the schema repository's docs/roadmap-evidence/fixed-<leg>.sexp). The lander now resolves a merge whose every conflicted path is in the one ledger set (cardgen.LedgerInPaths, which now names tla/COVERAGE.tsv): the keyed tables by their first column against the base (COVERAGE by machine, as RUNS and CASES by config), the roadmap data and the evidence ledgers by line and otherwise form by form (a fix by its id, a release block by its name, an evidence ledger as append-only history, every distinct form kept, including the schema repository's bare one-form-a-line ledgers the evidence decoder refused as trailing bytes), FIXES.md regenerated from the merged data. One id both sides change differently is refused naming it, and a code conflict is refused as before. tla/LandLedgers.tla holds CodeConflictNeverLands with three reversed witnesses. ## v1.2.14 (planned, 2026-10-11)

The next small fixes, one concern each, including the defects v1.2.12's tests find, a circuit breaker on the review loop, and a red base pushed to the coordinator.

- **What an operator reads matches the bare-merge refusal and the key rest** (planned). A late-merge judgment prints land for a real store and the bare merge only as the twin's form; the CLI, first-lap and test docs mark the bare merge twin-only (play is a twin tool); the spec and comments say a key rest ends only by routes wake, never by funded or a payment, and a test shows a balance poll cannot end one. From: readers' notes on nova-sprint PR #49 and PR #50.
- **A hook stays live while its re-challenge is in bound** (planned). The record's Live was the proof's bound alone, so a seat answering in time was refused HookFirst between the proof's Live and a re-challenge's own bound whenever a slow look sent the challenge late. The server now moves Live to the re-challenge's own bound through the record's one writer; a write that fails keeps the earlier bound (the safe side) and says so on the server's line. Test: TestARechallengeKeepsTheHookLiveUntilItsOwnBound. From: v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D6; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **doctor --preflight refuses a bench with no mirror for a repository the cards land on** (planned). The gate had no row for a repository a bench cannot stage. The set is PendingRepos: the distinct repositories of the sprint's not-yet-landed work cards and the streams' recorded repositories, as the name a member names its mirror (the last path segment without .git or -mirror, pkg/swarm FindBenchMirror's repoName). Each member's probe now prints one 'mirror <name> <path|->' line per repository from the same candidates FindBenchMirror tries, in its order, and parseProbe reads them into MemberProbe.Mirrors. Under doctor --preflight every member and repository with no mirror is one FAIL (area preflight, check mirrors, subject <member>/<repo>, remedy the loops play nova-tools' fleet/loops.yml, whose mirror-refresh row keeps ~/nova-bench/mirror/<repo>.git fresh), so the switch is refused; without --preflight the same fact is one WARN per member in member-env; a probe that did not measure mirrors (nil MemberProbe.Mirrors) judges none. docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md (doctor) states the row. From: tmp/next-sprint-cards/TOOLING-FROM-THE-SEAT-2026-10-11.md item 20; on 2026-10-11 the coordinator's own machine refused nova-sprint cards with "no bench mirror for <repo>".
- **brief check runs every add check without a write** (planned). An add's refusals arrived one class at a time, so a brief writer learned of the next only after fixing the last. The new read-only verb brief check runs every check add runs, in add's order, over every brief, and collects every finding: the id, the size bound, shared PATHS, the card lint, the WHO, base, TLA+ records, card checks, brief-base, paths-admit and sprint-base holds, then the add step's own plan on one read-only snapshot. It prints one CHECK line a finding and a BRIEF CHECK files=<n> findings=<m> line, --json prints the findings as one array, exits 0 with no finding, 1 with any, 2 for usage or an unreadable file, and 3 when the store does not answer and the store-free checks found nothing. Nothing is written and the brief decision is never asked. Tests: the twin store names two findings of three briefs in one call and leaves its keys equal, the clean brief is exit 0, and a brief over the size bound and a lint finding in one file are both said. From: tmp/next-sprint-cards/TOOLING-FROM-THE-SEAT-2026-10-11.md item 2; the owner, 2026-10-11.
- **add --partial holds back what fails and admits the rest** (planned). add was all or none: one failing brief refused the whole call, so the coordinator looped add, read the refusals, moved the refused files aside and added again. add --partial, with --brief-dir or a repeated --brief-file only, runs brief check's collector over every brief, holds back every brief with a finding and every card that needs a held card through its Needs: or DEPENDS-ON: line or --needs, transitively, then runs the add step's own plan over the rest and holds back each card its Refused list names with the cards that need it, planning the write again without them; the rounds are bounded by the number of cards, and nothing is written for a held card. The rest are admitted in one store write, the brief decision asked for them only. It prints one HELD <id>: <its first finding or refusal> or HELD <id>: needs <other>, held back line per held card, then the add's closing line, and exits 0 when every card was admitted, 1 when some were held and the rest written, and 2 when none could be admitted or for usage. --partial is refused with ids, --count, --sentinel or --land-protected, since a marked first add is one step. Without --partial add is all or none as before. Tests: five briefs, b2 with a PRIORITY add refuses and b4 DEPENDS-ON b2, admit b1, b3 and b5, hold b2 and b4 with their two lines, exit 1, and leave exactly three new cards; a brief the plan refuses at the write is held with its refusal and the others land; with every brief clean the exit is 0, as add without the flag. From: the seat's v1.2.14 audit, 2026-10-11 (TickIdle says "working again" when width is 0), checked against nova-sprint main 00c54ba; this card.
- **backup --out passes on a fleet that is beating** (planned). The restore check sets aside what a live member's beat rewrites while the dump is taken (the fleet table's revision, a fleet row's place, load text and up or down status) and compares everything else exactly, so a running fleet no longer fails the check; a held status, a missing row or a changed card still does. From: pre-clear backup, 2026-10-10 (8 fleet parts differed).
- **Card lint refuses valid cards: make gates and text inside fenced blocks** (planned). Card lint rejects make-driven gates and flags parent paths or absolute paths quoted inside fenced blocks. It should accept both. From: issue #1994; issue #2302; issue #3470.
- **One column field every reader agrees on** (planned). Card output carries a single column field so a card's state is not confused with the state of its need. From: card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04).
- **A stream has a display name** (planned). A stream's key stays its name everywhere (the work and merge rows, the stream= fields, every verb), and gains a human label: `stream set <s> --display <name>` records one line of printable text, at most 60 bytes, on the stream's control card as its `display` field, cleared with `default` or `none` like every other stream field. The dashboard's Work table and the streams listing show the display name when set, else `point-fix-<release>` when the stream belongs to a release, else the key (sprint.StreamDisplay); the streams verb prints it beside the release, StreamClock and StreamRow carry it in `Display`, and a name over the bound or with a newline is refused whole, nothing written. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: "agree that the name becomes the key, and you add a small display name. good tidy feature. pls add.".
- **A review loop has a circuit breaker** (planned). A card is escalated to the coordinator after 4 consecutive review rounds that each bring a new blocking finding, or after 6 substantive review rounds of any kind, instead of going round again. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai).
- **A red base is pushed to the coordinator** (planned). When the base a card lands onto is red, the machine pushes the coordinator a judgment naming the base and its red run. This is the push half of card a-landing-never-goes-onto-a-red-base; the landing gate itself stays in v1.3. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai).
- **An acknowledged empty row is one episode while it holds** (planned). emptyConds keys the empty-row episode by its text, and the text was rebuilt from the cards waiting once the judgment no longer sat in Open, so a second ready card she could do changed the text, wrote a second NFriendEmpty judgment and closed the acknowledgement, though the conjunction (she is up, her row empty, cards she could do wait) never cleared. The episode's text now comes from the judgment the coordinator holds (an acknowledgement, or a wait not yet due) as well as from an open one, so tla/CoordinatorPass.tla's OneJudgmentAnEpisode (Kind = "empty") holds in the code: the acknowledged episode stays one until the condition clears, a card dealt to her closes it, and a later episode is judged afresh past EmptyRowAfter. From: v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D9; this card.
- **A landing refuses a tla/*.cfg the case plan does not name** (planned). The lander's run-record check held the plan only to its own fields, so a head adding tla/MCFoo.cfg with no tla/CASES.tsv row, or taking a row for a configuration that stays, passed until tlacheck refused the whole plan. recordsRefusals now holds the merged tree to tlacheck's own loader, tlc.LoadCases, after ParseCases, and refuses with one line on tla/CASES.tsv; a tla/CASES.tsv edit alone holds a tree that carries models to its plan. LoadCases names, in name order, every MC*.cfg the plan does not name, every config the plan names that has no file, and every row whose module is missing, keeping its opening words. From: the seat, 2026-10-11, epoch 16; this card.
- **The page lock's comment-only check reads the page a browser renders** (planned). The stripper that proves a comment-only change renders nothing no longer mistakes four visible things for comments: an HTML text comment leaves nothing rather than a space; a comment opener inside a quoted attribute value is code; an inline script with a data-src attribute is read as JS; and a slash after a control if, while or for condition opens a regex, failing closed otherwise. The lock's header and the spec's The page lock state the comment-only form and that the card lint is ask-only. From: this card.
- **verify compares the scope its tree was imported with, not the whole organization** (planned). import --repo <org>/<name> now records the repositories it read as the work-tree's :scope, written only for a scoped import; a whole-organization tree stays byte for byte what it was, and a file without :scope reads as a whole-organization tree. verify with no --repo compares the tree's own scope (tla/WorkImport.tla's Verify already read the scope it imported), --repo narrows within it, and a --repo outside it is refused naming the scope before any GitHub call; verify --against does the same. Before, verify with no --repo read the whole organization and reported MISSING for every repository the scoped import left out. From: the card verify-defaults-to-the-trees-import-scope w2; the v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11 section 9 row D12 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **Every producer card has its consumer out after the tick** (planned). Adds ConsumersOut check at the end of every tick to assert that every producer card (working, fix, review) has its consumer out: an attempt held by an up member/friend for working/fix, or reads asked by up readers for review. Violations are reported as quiet judgments. Also reduces MaxSettle from 64 to 32 as per the owner's design, and changes settle bound handling to push a judgment instead of erroring the tick. From: the owner, 2026-10-11 ~10:40-11:00 AM ET, on the live epoch 17; card every-producer-card-has-its-consumer-out-after-the-tick.w1.
- **DirtyTick models ConsumersOut at each tick's end** (planned). tla/DirtyTick.tla gains ConsumersOut, an action property checked at each tick's end: every working card's attempt is held by a machine up, every review card's read is held by a reader up (unless judged stranded, no route, at its bound, or its read already said ok), and every ready card a route serves and a free up slot could take is dealt in the same tick. The fix "consumersout" re-pumps the work table in the settle loop (sub-ticks until the consumer queue is empty, bound MaxSub 32, reaching it a judgment SettleBoundJudged). tla/MCDirtyTickConsumers.tla and .cfg (width 2) check it, with four reversed witnesses (a deal of one card per tick, a settle loop cut after one sub-tick, a read asked in the next tick instead of this one, a member-down whose attempts are not re-dealt) that TLC must fail. From: the owner, 2026-10-11 ~10:40-11:00 AM ET, on the live epoch 17; card tla-dirtytick-consumers-out-at-the-tick-end-2.w7; continued by card tla-dirtytick-consumers-out-at-the-tick-end-2.w9.
- **The ready-over judgment reads the deal's settled rests** (planned). A ready card whose tier is served only by a route resting at the tick's now raises the ready-over judgment (a ready card is not dealt), naming the resting route, whether the provider's recorded rest or one the rule rests this tick. The ready-over part settles the rests once as the deal does (withRests), on the snapshot the conditions are counted on, so the route the judgment names as resting is exactly one the deal does not draw; a rest whose time has ended is not named and the card is dealt. From: card ready-over-reads-the-settled-rests.w2; the seat's v1.2.14 audit, 2026-10-11.
- **The ready-over judgment is keyed on the cause, never its figures** (planned). The ready-over judgment is one per (reason, tier), keyed by the reason the deal leaves the card (condKey's NReadyOver case, readyOverWhy). The reason names figures that move while the cause stands -- a route's balance (out of budget (balance $x)) and a rest's end (resting until <stamp>) -- so as the balance moved the key changed, notify closed the old judgment and wrote a second one: one cause, a second push, and the coordinator's wait on the first lost. readyOverWhy now takes each moving figure out of the key before keying, while the What keeps it, so the judgment is rewritten in place with the latest figures and pushed once. From: the coordinator, 2026-10-11 (v1.2.14 defect ready-over-key-ignores-the-balance-amount); checked against nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **run refuses a negative --tick-deadline** (planned). A negative --tick-deadline is refused right after the flags are parsed, through run's usual refuse helper, before the loop starts or a server listens; the refusal names the flag, the value and that 0 waits for ever. Before, tickDeadlineOf returned 0 for any least <= 0 and tickWithin waited for ever when d <= 0, so --tick-deadline -1s switched the watchdog off with nothing said. 0 still waits for ever and every positive value behaves as today. From: nova-tools#5173 (transferred here at the split), roadmap item tick-watchdog-bounded-diagnostics, its negative-deadline half; this card.
- **The tick watchdog never waits on its own dump** (planned). An overrun's goroutine stacks are written into memory first (pprof's WriteTo into a bytes.Buffer, which cannot block), then the watchdog acts (the tick's cancel, or the wedged exit), and only then hands the buffer to stderr in a goroutine it waits on at most TickStacksBound (2 s); a stderr nobody drains (a full pipe under a supervisor, a blocked terminal) can no longer hold up the cancel or the exit, and a dump not written within the bound is dropped with one TICK STACKS line saying so. From: the card tick-watchdog-exit-never-waits-on-its-dump w2; nova-tools issue #5173, roadmap item tick-watchdog-bounded-diagnostics; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **The stops digest counts only the stops still holding** (planned). One plan could close a stop and at the same time send an NStopsDigest saying it still holds: notify closes the open NStopMemberDown judgment of a member up again, and stopsDigest then gathered its stops from the snapshot before the plan, counting and naming the stop just closed. stopsDigest now leaves out every judgment the same plan closes, matched by note id; with no stop left it writes neither the digest nor its clock. From: v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D8; card stops-digest-counts-only-held-stops.w1, id given by the coordinator 2026-10-11 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **init over a keyless store records the seat move, so an earlier observation lapses** (planned). init writing a coordinator name onto a store whose key holds none while a friend-health record survives (an observation made under an earlier seat) now records the move as a seat change, as the seat's own step does: the seat record and its generation stepped, written with the key, its log line and its note, so the earlier observation lapses by FriendEvidence's generation check. A fresh store's first init writes no seat record, and init over a held key keeps the holder, as before. From: this card; v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11 section 9 row D10 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **The lander's empty-commit refusal says a result is missing when it holds none** (planned). The lander's empty-commit check refused an empty diff with no result to read (a nil work card: the fleet row absent or the work card tidied away) with the same finding as one whose result claimed changes, "empty commit: the result claims changes the diff does not show", naming a claim nothing made. It now returns emptyCommitNoResultFinding, "empty commit: the head changes nothing from the attempt's start, and the lander holds no result to say why", and both findings return the card to review through one helper, isEmptyCommitFinding. From: this card: lander-empty-commit-says-no-result-is-held, from the v1.2.14 point-release plan and the roadmap item lander-empty-commit-handling.
- **A hook push is sent only once its record names it** (planned). When the hook record write fails, a look now delivers none of that look's pushes and undoes what it added (the note keys it marked sent, the pushes it added to the open list, and the sequence), so the next look offers them again, records them, and sends them once. The SEAT HOOK line it prints is unchanged. Before, the push was delivered while the record named no unacknowledged push, so a push delivered over a failed record write never blocked the gate: past HookAckBound a coordinator command ran though the push had been delivered and was never recorded. From: the card a-hook-push-is-sent-only-once-recorded w1; the v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11 section 9 row D7 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **A machine's fault down keeps another's hold mark** (planned). When presence takes a member down for a missed beat, the machine writes its own fault hold (held_by=fault, fault_since) only on a member that carries no hold: a member the sync, the adopt, its environment or the coordinator already holds keeps its hold, its mark, its reason and its finish marker when it goes down, and still goes down. Overwriting the mark hid the hold from its own release, so a held member could no longer be released and the clear left a markless hold (tla/DealFill.tla FaultHold and PersonHoldStays; docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 5). From: the seat's audit, 2026-10-11 (a reader finding on card a-member-environment-fault-holds-it-and-pushes-the-seatb, attempt 5, head 38c66ea7542f); this card.
- **A load over more than one read set reads the table's mark** (planned). readInto read a table of more than ntable.LimitReadSetMembers records in several read sets and checked only that each saw the table's revision, so a store that lost writes and wrote others up to the same revision between two read sets (a restart from an older save, a failover) gave one revision and two histories and the load mixed them. It now reads the mark of the change event that left the table's revision (TableChangesMarked, as markOf reads it) before the first read set and after the last, and a mark that changed is a movedError, as a changed revision is, so the load reads again under its existing retry. A table of at most 1024 records, or a backend that keeps no marks, reads as before (tla/LoadCache.tla, LoadIsSnapshot). From: the v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D5; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **The version verb says which fixes a build carries** (planned). nova-sprint version --features lists the fixes this build carries, one line each `<release> <fix-id> <title>`, from the fixes ledger compiled into the binary (docs/embed.go) and read with make roadmap's parser: every fix of a release at or below the build's version. A build whose version is not a release (a dev build) lists the shipped releases' fixes and says the unreleased fixes of the tree it was built from are not listed. nova-sprint version --has <fix-id> exits 0 when the build carries the fix and 1 when the ledger names it in a later release or not at all, naming which; --json prints {version, fixes:[{release,id,title}]}. From: tmp/next-sprint-cards/TOOLING-FROM-THE-SEAT-2026-10-11.md item 16 (the owner, 2026-10-11); the v1.2.10 bisect, where the coordinator ran strings on two binaries to learn whether v1.2.9 held the environment-fault fix.
- **A stats reset zeroes the unattributed spend** (planned). After nova-sprint stats reset every stream's spend counts from the mark, but the grand total did not reach zero: the cost line's <other>, the largest TierCosts.Unreconciled on any stream's record, is the sprint's UnreconciledSpend since the epoch's clear, never since the mark. ResetMark now holds the sprint's unattributed spend at the mark (in cents) and streamsSince subtracts it on every stream's record, the streams the mark does not know included, so the cost line, the dashboard's cost tile and where --json's unreconciled count from the mark, never below zero. The mark line names it beside the total. From: the seat's v1.2.14 audit, 2026-10-11 (a stats reset does not zero the grand total spent), checked against nova-sprint main 00c54ba; the owner's rule of 2026-10-09: a stats reset clears every cost figure, the total spent, per card and per tier; this card a-stats-reset-zeroes-the-unattributed-spend.
- **A stale post-STOP beat keeps its word for the settle** (planned). settleStopDebtByBeat read a machine's live set fresh-only (sprint.LiveNamesAt through liveOf), so a machine that beat once after the STOP naming its held report and then went silent past BeatDeadline had its lease settled at START: the card went back to ready at gen+1, was dealt again, and the held report was refused as stale when it came. The owner's last beat since the STOP now keeps its word fresh or stale (sprint.LiveNamedAt, no clock), as tla/StopReturn.tla SettleByBeat reads it (d.id \notin beat); tla/LiveRuns.tla's reversed witness "staleasabsent" is exactly that wrong reading: a silent row's stale beat as an empty live set. LiveNamesAt, LiveHeldAt, liveOf and LiveReturns keep their fresh-only reading. No model change. From: the coordinator 2026-10-11, added to v1.2.14 beside the v1.2.12 inventory's section 9 row D2 (a held finished report across STOP refused as stale); D2's first cause was fixed by nova-sprint #87 (15c779c); this is what that fix left; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **Every held_by write names a hold mark, and each mark keeps the member off the deal** (planned). Tests only, no product change. internal/sprint/hold_marks_test.go holds a table of every mark a member's held_by carries -- none (the coordinator's), the sync's, the machine's fault, the adopt's and the environment's -- each written by its own writer (a fleet hold with its HeldBy, presence's down for the fault, holdAdopting for the adopt, a finish whose report is an environment fault for envFaulted) and cleared by its own release (fleet up, the sync's release, faultClear, clearEnvFault, the adopt's finish). For each it pins the behaviour: the member is not up and dealt no card by the deal or the level, a tick presence with a fresh beat leaves held and held_by as they were, another mark's mark-scoped release leaves it held with its mark, and its own release clears it. It then scans the package's non-test .go files for every held_by assignment (a name[FieldHeldBy] = X and FieldHeldBy: X) and fails naming the value and its file:line when no table row names it, so a new hold kind cannot ship without the table checked against it. The known-yes proof is envFaulted's status line deleted: the environment row then fails at UpMembers. From: this card, card-lint-a-hold-owner-every-reader-accepts.w1, from the reader finding on a-member-environment-fault-holds-it-and-pushes-the-seatb attempt 5 (head 38c66ea7542f): the environment hold was written with held_by=environment but the member's status was left Up, so the level dealt to it and presence wrote held_by=fault over the mark.
- **A brief edit records its needs, and the deal refuses a card whose needs have not landed** (planned). A card's needs are only the column's, not the brief's: brief re-points needs only through dependsOnly (the DEPENDS-ON line the only difference), and any other edit took the ordinary path, wrote the brief and dropped the parsed needs, so on 2026-10-11 a brief --dir moved 85 briefs that now carry DEPENDS-ON while every card kept zero needs and stayed ready; and dealPlan's eligibility checked stream held, friend pin and inState(c, Ready) only, no guard on needs, so a ready card with unlanded needs was dealt. Now the ordinary brief path writes the needs the new brief's DEPENDS-ON names whenever they differ from the card's, clearing them when the brief drops its DEPENDS-ON; a ready card that gains a need not landed moves ready -> waiting in the same unit (the lifecycle accepts the move, ready -> waiting being no longer only a sentinel's effect when the edit records needs); dealPlan refuses a card with WaitsFor(s, c, nil) non-empty, and unmet judges every move to dealt (Working) against the card's stored needs, so Lawful refuses dealing a card whose needs have not landed whatever path asks for it; a card dealt or working keeps its attempt and the new needs apply from its next deal. help brief says this. Red tests in internal/sprint/needs_guard_test.go (a ready card whose brief gains an unlanded need waits with its needs recorded; a waiting or ready card whose edit names landed needs stays or becomes ready; a ready card with an unlanded need built in the store is never dealt and the tick's invariant names it; an edit with no needs change leaves them; a brief that drops its DEPENDS-ON clears the card's needs). The invariant a primary anywhere but waiting has every need landed already named such a card; this is the deal and the brief catching up (docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, needs and the deal). From: this card, a-brief-edit-records-its-needs-and-the-deal-checks-them.w3, from the owner on the live epoch 17, 2026-10-11 ~10:40-11:00 AM ET: 89 v1212 cards ran or sat ready before their DEPENDS-ON landed (four failed four attempts each); code read at nova-sprint main 1405d26; the owner: "by definition this must not happen.".
- **The card lint refuses a header key below the prose** (planned). cardHeaderBlock ends the card header at the first prose line ("ended = true // the prose begins here") and CardHeaderValue reads only that block, so a header key written below the prose was never read and nothing said so: only the five typed keys (KIND, PATHS, TEST, LEGS, SOURCE) drew a stranded finding. A new swarm.LintHeaderStranded reuses cardHeaderBlock and returns one finding per header key (KIND, PATHS, TEST, LEGS, SOURCE, START, STOP, DEPENDS-ON, PRIORITY, NEW, SHARED, REPO, BASE, RESULT, tier) written as a KEY: line below the block, naming the key and its line; a key in the header passes and a sentence that merely mentions a key mid-line draws nothing. lintBriefReads calls it, so add, brief, recut and preflight refuse a stranded key through the same path as every other lint finding, exit 2 (preflight exit 1), nothing written. LintCardDepends (which nothing outside tests called) is deleted; its stranded-DEPENDS-ON finding is now this one, and the package doc and lineup helpers (Lineup, CardDependsRemedy, ReadLineup and their exclusive readers) that only it used are removed with it. This is the bug behind the 2026-10-11 epoch 17: 89 v1212 briefs carried DEPENDS-ON: below the REPO:/BASE: sentence, briefNeeds read no needs from any of them, add admitted every card straight to ready, and cards were dealt before their dependencies landed. From: this card: card-lint-refuses-a-header-key-below-the-prose, from the owner on epoch 17, 2026-10-11 (~10:40-11:00 AM ET); code read by the seat's reader at nova-sprint main 1405d26; the owner: "this should be caught by card lint.".
- **needs set re-points a card's needs in place** (planned). The only way to change a card's needs after admission was drop and re-add, so a card admitted with the wrong needs needed a twin. A card's needs are read once at add (briefNeeds) and a brief edit drops them on any change beyond the DEPENDS-ON line, and on 2026-10-11 ~100 frontier cards could not be re-pointed or reworked without twins. Now nova-sprint needs set <id> (--needs <a,b> | --clear) [--answers <note>] is the direct verb, the coordinator's alone: it rewrites the line the brief names its needs on (Needs: or DEPENDS-ON:, keeping that line's key; --clear takes the line off; a brief with no such line gains a DEPENDS-ON: line) so card <id> shows the truth, and it moves the card by the one lifecycle table: a ready card that gains a need not landed moves ready -> waiting, a waiting card whose new needs have all landed moves waiting -> ready, a card working or in review keeps its attempt with the new needs applying from its next deal (the brief edit's briefDepends path), and a landed or off-table card, a sentinel, and a need that is no primary on the table (named whole) are refused, exit 1, nothing written. The path is chosen by the card's column, not by whether it has ever been dealt: a card returned to waiting or ready in place after an attempt takes the lifecycle move and keeps its attempt field, so it is never sent to drop and re-add a twin. unmet now judges a move waiting -> ready by the needs the unit writes, not the ones the pre-state holds. help needs names it (docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, needs). Red tests in cmd/nova-sprint/needs_set_test.go pin all seven: ready -> waiting with the move printed, waiting -> ready on landed needs, --clear emptying a waiting card to ready, a need not on the table refused naming it with nothing written, a dealt card keeping its attempt, a landed and a dropped card refused, and the brief's DEPENDS-ON line rewritten with no other line changed. From: this card: needs-set-repoints-a-cards-needs-in-place.w3 (attempts 1-2 carried), from the owner on the live epoch 17, 2026-10-11 ~11:25 AM ET ("I hate twins." / "Twinning is the last refuge of the scoundrel. Fix your tools."); code read at nova-sprint main 1405d26; seat tooling item 26.
- **A read is never asked onto a resting route while another of its tier serves** (planned). readRouteOf (internal/sprint/route.go), which draws a read card's route from the read tier's array, built its served set from every enabled route of the tier and left out only avoid (the routes a read of the primary returned on), so it never asked whether a route rests. The read-card ask could then put a read on a route resting for its 5xxs or its provider's credit, and the next pass's readCardsTakeBack retired it as RetiredByRest because cardRest said its route rests, while the ask put it back on the same route, so reads churned ask, retire, ask for as long as the rest held even though another route of the tier could serve. readRouteOf now leaves out the routes that rest at s.Now while another route of the tier serves, adding them to the set preferFirst avoids and holding them only while another entry remains drawable, so with every route of the read tier resting the ask draws the first as it did before and the take-back still handles it (no new refusal, no new judgment). readCardsAskFull settles the view's rests once with withRests() when it holds none, so no read scans the fleet table and s.resting sees them (docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 6, the reads; tla/RouteIndex.tla, THE READS). Red tests first in internal/sprint/read_route_rest_test.go, on a pro primary whose read tier's array is pro-a, pro-b: with pro-a resting (a 3-in-10 rule rest, and a rate-limit backoff from one rate-limited take record) the read the ask creates carries pro-b's FieldRoute, never pro-a's; with both routes resting the reads are still asked a route, as today. From: this card, a-read-is-never-asked-onto-a-resting-route.w1, from the fourth cold read of nova-sprint PR #86 (2026-10-11), an open non-blocking finding (readRouteOf ignores rests) listed in tmp/next-sprint-cards/rate-limit-never-fails-the-card-v2.md; checked on PR #86's head a1c51ee and on main 00c54ba, where readRouteOf is at route.go:813 and holds for every rest, not only a backoff.
- **A friend that serves a tier counts as its route** (planned). Whether a tier is served is one question with one answer: tierServed says a tier is served by an enabled, unrested route of it, or by a friend row up and unheld whose tiers include it (a member row likewise when the fleet's tiers allow), and every site that validates a tier reads it. routeTier's frontier branch refused every frontier card before it consulted the check, so rework of a frontier card was refused, held.go and idle.go raised "no route serves tier frontier", readers.go and ready_over.go read the same words as its cause, and judgments_retire.go retired the judgment only when a route appeared, while the friends' deal already handed frontier cards to a friend row whose tiers include frontier. A frontier card is now the friends' by design: a friend up whose row lists frontier serves it as a route would, and with no such friend the refusal names both the routes and the friends it looked at. docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, tiers and routes, says it. Tests: TestReworkAcceptsAFrontierTierAFriendServes, TestAcceptSeesAFrontierTierAFriendServes, TestIdleRootForAFrontierTierAFriendServesIsNoNoRoute, TestAFrontierTierNoFriendServesIsRefused, TestAFrontierTierAFriendServesRaisesNoNoRouteJudgment. From: this card; the owner, 2026-10-11 ~11:25 AM ET, on the live epoch 17: "I hate twins." / "Twinning is the last refuge of the scoundrel. Fix your tools."; code read at nova-sprint main 1405d26.
- **The dashboard plays a gentle coin when a tick lands a card** (planned). The dashboard at :7390 gains one sound and nothing else, on the owner's ask: when a refresh's page copy carries a landed count higher than the refresh before's, the page plays one short coin -- two sine partials, the second a fifth above the first, about 0.25 s, a fast decay, peak gain 0.15 -- synthesized in app.js with WebAudio, so no audio file joins the repository and the page makes no extra request. It plays once per refresh however many landed in it, never on the first load and never when the count falls (a clear); the tick id the read carried is the copy's at, so two reads of one tick play nothing. A browser refuses audio before a gesture, so the page carries one small speaker glyph beside the landed count, off until clicked once per browser (the choice kept in localStorage); clicked on, it plays the coin once, as the test. One paragraph in docs/SPEC-SPRINT-DASHBOARD.md, "The coin", and the lock's ask line with pagelock.txt's digest. - **A 5xx whose words mention a rate limit still spends the take and rests the route** (planned). On a limited route the finish then took the rate-limited return in internal/sprint/steps_work.go: the card went back unspent, with no FieldTakeEnded and no provider take record, so transient() never counted it, and three such 5xxs in ten never rested the route for RouteRestFor, reading a real outage as a brief backoff. Now, when the line parses a class of class5xx or classTimeout, only class=rate-limited or status=429 makes it a rate limit and the word fallback is skipped; a line with no parsed class, or another class, keeps the word fallback. - **A rate limit stalls its route briefly; it never fails a card or rests it for 3-in-10** (planned). A take a provider ends rate-limited (class=rate-limited) never fails the card, on any route and however many times: the card returns unspent (no FieldTakeEnded, no redeal, no attempt, no failed-work judgment, none of the out-of-credit bound FieldRateReturns) and leaves a rate_take_<n> record numbered after the last one the card holds, with no gap and no bound, so RateTakes reads every one. The route backs off briefly, then serves again by itself: RestsDue computes the backoff purely from those records, k being the route's rate-limited ends since its last ok end (a take the worker finished ok, in the finished cell or past it; a failed finish resets nothing) and last the latest one's time, ending at last + min(60s*2^(k-1), 15m) (RateBackoff) -- a fixed point in time, never relative to now. Its line is kept beside the route's own rest in the provider's rule3_rest_ property (<route>+rate-backoff), never over it, so it never moves the 3-in-10 window's mark, never blocks the coordinator's rest and is never woken; a backoff on every route of a tier makes the card wait ready, as a provider at its concurrency budget does, never a no-route judgment, and the no-stall rule holds it on the backoff whenever a route of the tier backs off and none can be drawn (never NStalled); the rebalance never moves a card onto a machine with no route it can draw; restWrites writes it and one happened note ("rate-limit backoff of <d> on <route>, until <t>") once per end, none while the same end holds, never a judgment, and drops a backoff line once its end has passed. A rate limit no longer counts toward the 3-in-10 transient rest (transient excludes classRateLimited); a 5xx window still rests the route 30 minutes, and is written over a backoff that holds. member.Judge treats a rate-limited run with no pushed head as a provider failure whatever its shape, while a shaped result that pushed a head stays the card's own. TLA+ model RateBackoff, properties RateLimitSpendsNoRedeal and BackoffBounded with the temporal BackoffEnds, reversed witnesses MCRateBackoffBrokenSpend and MCRateBackoffBrokenNoCap. ## v1.2.15 (planned)

The next small product fixes, one concern each.

- **The landing gate runs its classes side by side** (planned). Every landing gate ran sprint.BaseClasses one class after another: build, gofmt, vet, vet -tags functional, then three separate `go test` processes for the internal/ci analyzer classes (staticcheck, errcheck, dead-code), then class-tests and the unit packages. The two vets and the analyzer tests only read the tree and none depends on another's output. The three analyzer classes are now one `go test -tags functional -count=1 -timeout 600s -run '^(TestStaticcheckFindings|TestUncheckedErrors|TestDeadCode)$' ./internal/ci/` run, one test binary for the tree, and a red one is attributed to the class its `--- FAIL:` line names. A class carries a Stage int (0 build; 1 gofmt, vet, vet-functional, analyzers; 2 class-tests and unit); gateRuns returns the runs by stage, the local gate runs each stage's runs concurrently, waits the stage and reports the first red in class order (not finish order), and the bench gate runs each stage's runs as background jobs and prints them in class order. The report order is the class order. From: this card, the-landing-gate-runs-its-classes-side-by-side.w2; the owner, 2026-10-11: "What else is like serial reads, going out one at a time, when they could go out at the same time in || ?" and "log critical cards to fix all these serial things that should be parallel"; found by the seat's audit child on nova-sprint main.
- **Run independent TLC cases in a bounded parallel pool** (planned). RunSuite gives each selected case its own Java process, scratch and log while a bounded worker pool runs independent cases concurrently. `--parallel` defaults to one quarter of the bench CPUs and refuses widths above half; Makefile tlc and tlc-full pass TLC_PARALLEL when set. Each result keeps its case wall time, records stay in plan order, and OnCase callbacks are serialized in completion order. The shared 110 second suite deadline and budget-exhausted records remain in force. The real land group passes at width one and the default width with identical PASS/FAIL results. From: this card, tlc-suite-runs-independent-cases-in-parallel.w1~17.g7, 2026-10-11.
- **A land pass pushes each repository and base on its own lane** (planned). A land pass merged and gated streams side by side (phase 1), then landed every built batch from one serial loop across every repository and every base: while one batch rebuilt and ran a combined tree gate (minutes), a built batch of another repository or another base waited, and the same goroutine prepared each next job. Phase 2 now runs one landing lane per (clone, base): each lane is a goroutine with its own ready list and its own pushed list, ordered by stream priority and landGrace exactly as the one loop ordered them, and pushes its batches one at a time; different clones, and different bases of one clone, share no ref and no tip, so their pushes run side by side (serial within one base is the design and stays, tla/LandPass.tla). The job's prepare runs in its own goroutine, the first cuts of one repository and base still in priority order; the fetch lock becomes one lock per clone, keyed on the clone's own directory (fetchKey, the parent of its common git dir), so a fetch in a stream's worktree takes the same lock as the clone's own worktree writes: two clones' fetches and worktree writes go side by side while one clone's stay serial; failed and the queues are updated under one mutex. The key is stable across the clone's own creation (it was the directory before `git clone` made it and the common git dir after, so two lanes of one repository could take two locks and prepare a half-made clone; attempt 8 keys on the clone directory, the common git dir's parent). The landing order within one base and every message are unchanged. From: this card, a-landing-pushes-each-repo-and-base-on-its-own-lane.w5; the owner, 2026-10-11: "What else is like serial reads, going out one at a time, when they could go out at the same time in || ?" and "OK please log critical cards to fix all these serial things that should be parallel (with good reason to be ||)."; found by the seat's audit child on nova-sprint main the same day (cmd/nova-sprint/landpass.go, THE LANDINGS, SERIAL); attempt 8 fixes the clone-creation key a reader found (land.go, clone).
